title: Quickstart Gateway: adaptive hero mosaic & context-aware step snapshots
creator: Avery Chen
description: Scope: Refresh the Quickstart landing hero and above-the-fold visual system to support progressive discovery for first-run users. Deliverables include: 1) adaptive hero mosaic (3 viewport variants: mobile, tablet, desktop) with layered screenshot placeholders and motion states; 2) a set of 6 contextual step snapshots (task-driven thumbnails) that map to existing quickstart tasks (API key, first request, sample prompt, eval run, cost dashboard, invite teammate); 3) visual language tokens and a micro-copy guidance sheet for engineers to render consistent thumbnails in the app; 4) export-ready screenshot templates and an export checklist for product releases.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Figma master file has distinct frames for mobile/tablet/desktop hero with responsive layout constraints and annotated handoff specs; 2) 6 step snapshot templates exported as PNG/SVG with exact dimensions for CMS and Console; 3) microcopy agreed with PM and applied to all variants; 4) engineering integration ticket created with links to assets and QA checklist; 5) accessibility pass: color contrast >= 4.5:1 for call-to-action text and descriptive alt text patterns documented.
design_decisions: - Use a modular mosaic composed of 3 layered cards: app screenshot, explanatory badge, and contextual blur background to create depth without photorealism. - Favor clipped, rounded-corner screenshot frames to match Console cards. - Motion should be subtle: parallax offset on desktop hero, fade-in stagger for step snapshots. - Avoid literal device mockups to keep imagery evergreen across rapid UI changes.
tradeoffs_and_risks: - Tradeoff: abstracted screenshots (placeholders + tokenized UI strips) reduce maintenance but may undercommunicate live UI fidelity for some customers. - Risk: hero motion could affect perceived performance on low-end devices; provide a static fallback and prefer CSS-based transforms. - Risk: timeline pressure may force single breakpoint-first approach; try to land desktop + mobile parity before release.
